title: Milneburg, Barbarin's Bourbon Street Parade and the Crescent City school band
summary: He recalls Milneburg, learning Paul Barbarin wrote Bourbon Street Parade, and his own school-friend band led by Bigfoot Bill.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Was Millenburg going when you were a boy?

Millenburg, yes. That's where they used to go out on the beach down, Millenburg, and I think that's where the song more or less was derived from, this Millenburg joy. Yeah. And it was a funny thing. I didn't know, as much as I had played with Paul Barber, and I just found out not too long ago that he had written this number, the Bourbon Street Parade. I didn't know that. You didn't remember that? No, it did not until I went down to Jazz Limited one night. I talked to Freddie Coleman and another buddy of mine was down there, I worked with him in New Orleans, his name was Warden Joseph, trombone man, and they called him Frog. Yeah. Well we happened to be talking and they asked him, I said, what's the name of this last number you played? They said, well that's the Bourbon Street Parade. I said, Bourbon Street Parade. So I said, whose number is that? He said, Paul's number. And I was so surprised I didn't know what to do because they didn't know. Well to begin with, when he organized, he wasn't playing them kind of tunes. Because he had written some tunes I think when he was in New York with Lois Russell's band.
When I came back, Sweet Papa. Yeah. A couple of others.
And well I remember one particular one that we used to use as a theme song, which was called I think, To Your Picture in the Frame.

I don't know what I've heard of. Yeah. Your picture in the frame. Well I remember that very well because of the fact that we used to open up all the dance engagements with it. And I used to close, so therefore I remembered it very much. And when he came down there he got some of the fellas from the band I had been working with at the time. And this band was comprised of fellas that used to go to school together, you know, and we called ourselves and at Crescent City I had us. And we more or less took care of all the school engagements and what have you, and various parties and picnics we used to play. And we had one fella from the old school work with us for quite some time. And as a matter of fact he was in charge of ours. We made him in charge of this group since we thought he knew so much about it. And his name was Bigfoot Bill. I don't know whether you had the occasion to meet him or not, but he was a drummer. And he had played around New Orleans with several bands a long time ago. Now whether he was born in Ridd there or not I don't know, but I can remember he joined our group and he helped us quite a bit. And we had a piano player by the name of Wiggins, he was very nice.
Yeah he still plays at a place called Lutyens.
Well I'll tell you there were several fellas in the world.
With Toca, do you remember Lawrence Toca? Well that's not his real name, there's another name he has, a trumpet player. Lawrence Toca. He was very short, small, so. Lawrence Toca.
How did it came up later? He was not young.
